descriptors.definition: This approach involves automatically hedging currency exposures in the forward market as soon as they arise without regard to rate attractiveness. It secures known yields and costs with minimal cash flow destabilization and zero managerial effort, but fails to optimize transaction costs.
inclusion: Automatic booking of forward contracts for all exposures
Zero managerial effort for active monitoring
exclusion: Selective hedging based on rate predictions
nearby_distinctions: Differs from selective hedging by removing market timing entirely and hedging automatically regardless of rates.

descriptors.definition: This strategy entails selectively hedging exposures when forward rates are favorable while leaving them open when rates are unfavorable. It requires quantifying future market expectations, comparing hedged positions to bonds and unhedged positions to equities.
inclusion: Selective hedging based on attractive forward rates
Keeping exposures open when rates are unattractive
exclusion: Automatic uncritical hedging of every exposure
Continuous active trading of forward contracts
nearby_distinctions: Unlike automatic hedging, it incorporates market views and predictive accuracy to manage a mix of hedged and unhedged exposures.

descriptors.definition: This strategy leaves all foreign exchange exposures completely unhedged, resulting in zero expenditure of managerial time or effort. However, it carries a very high risk of cash flow destabilization due to currency volatility.
inclusion: Leaving all operational and financial currency exposures unhedged
nearby_distinctions: Unlike hedged strategies, it completely avoids transaction costs at the expense of maximum cash flow volatility.

descriptors.definition: This strategy involves active speculation in the currency market through continuous cancellations and re-bookings of forward contracts. It transforms the corporate trading function into a profit center under relaxed exchange controls.
inclusion: Continuous cancellation and re-booking of forward contracts
Treating the treasury function as a profit center
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard hedging by intentionally taking speculative market positions to generate profit rather than merely mitigating risk.

descriptors.definition: Globalization of financial markets and international trade increases exchange rate risk, volatility, and cross-border interdependence. Consequently, financial managers must understand these risk factors and apply appropriate risk reduction methods.
inclusion: Analysis of international trade and investment risk factors
nearby_distinctions: Serves as an overarching summary of macroeconomic drivers rather than a tactical hedging mechanism.
